conservation_statuses.status: Precautionary (illegal collection risk; salep trade threat)
conservation_statuses.description: Precautionary geoprivacy for Turkey due to documented, large-scale illegal harvesting of terrestrial, tuberous orchids for salep production. Harvesting involves uprooting the tuber, which kills the plant, and is explicitly prohibited under Turkish national law—yet continues at very high levels. CITES-cited estimates report ~30–120 million tubers collected annually, with documented population declines and local extinctions in some regions. Because precise locality disclosure can facilitate further collection, Turkey observations are obscured. Sources: CITES E-CoP19-Inf-09_1; Kühn & Pedersen (2019); Delforge (2006).

Precautionary location protection applied to limit dissemination of precise coordinates for a location-sensitive taxon potentially vulnerable to harvesting and illegal trade. All native orchid species are legally protected from international trade by listing under CITES Appendix II. Large scale wild harvesting (e.g., for salep production) has been documented as a pressure on certain populations in some Greek regions. This designation is intended as a risk-reduction measure only and does not represent a formal conservation assessment.

conservation_statuses.status: Precautionary (Strict National Protection / Illegal Harvesting Risk)
conservation_statuses.authority: Turkish Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry / CITES Appendix II
conservation_statuses.description: *All wild orchid species in Turkey* are subject to **strict national conservation laws** and **international trade regulations**. Under the *Regulation on Harvesting, Production, and Export of Flower Bulbs* (Official Gazette No. 22371) and the *Turkish Penal Code*, the **unauthorized uprooting, collection, or damaging of wild orchids and their underground parts is strictly prohibited**. As all members of *Orchidinae* are listed under **CITES Appendix II**, and **precise locality data** has been documented to facilitate **illegal extraction in violation of national law**, geoprivacy is **obscured** to ensure compliance with Turkish conservation mandates and to **prevent the unauthorized removal of protected biological resources**.

conservation_statuses.authority: Hellenic Ministry of Environment & Energy (CITES Management Authority) / CITES Secretariat
conservation_statuses.description: Precautionary location protection applied to limit dissemination of precise coordinates for a location-sensitive taxon potentially vulnerable to targeted disturbance. Native orchid species occurring in Greece are protected under Presidential Decree 67/1981 (national), Council Regulation (EC) No 338/97 (European Union), and CITES Appendix II (international). Wild harvesting of orchids (e.g. for salep production) has been documented as a pressure on certain populations. This designation is intended as a risk-reduction measure only and does not represent a formal conservation assessment.

page.title: Orchis anthropophora
page.extract:
Orchis anthropophora (formerly Aceras anthropophorum), the man orchid, is a European species of orchid whose flowers resemble a human figure. The head is formed by the petals and sepals, and the suspended torso and limbs by the lobes of the labellum. It usually grows in calcareous grassland.


== Description ==
The man orchid is a herbaceous perennial, growing to a height of 20 to 40 cm (7.9 to 16 in). A basal rosette of 5 cm (2.0 in) lanceolate leaves develops from a tuber 6 cm (2.4 in) in diameter, and between April and June a central flower spike is produced bearing up to fifty small, stemless flowers – the flowers vary from greenish, with a yellow-green labellum, to green, streaked and marked with purple. 


== Habitat ==
Orchis anthropophora favours moderately sunny meadows on well-drained, often calcareous soil. It is to be found around the Mediterranean area, and in central and western Europe as far north as southern England. It also grows in alpine areas, but not at high altitude.
It is native to Great Britain, central Europe (Austria, Belgium, Germany, the Netherlands, and Switzerland), southwestern Europe (the Balearic Islands, Corsica, France, Portugal, Sardinia, and Spain), southeastern Europe (Albania, Greece, Italy, Crete, Sicily, and countries of the former Yugoslavia), northern Africa (Algeria, Morocco, and Tunisia), and western Asia (Cyprus, East Aegean Islands, Lebanon, Syria, and Turkey).
